atoms.obligation: Work through each required step of the process in order, treating every one as an obligation you can be held to.
atoms.lesson: This skill guides the ML engineer through a retraining end to end. Work the sections in order; each one names an obligation you can be held to. The document is organised as ten numbered sections followed by a closing checklist.

atoms.obligation: Split the evaluation data by time and by location group, never at random, when preparing to measure performance.
atoms.lesson:
The ML engineer owns this step.

Split by time and by site, never at random — random splits leak neighbouring pixels and adjacent dates into the test set and inflate every metric.
atoms.anchor: 1. Model retraining discipline for this retraining

atoms.obligation: Freeze the evaluation set before you touch, modify, or add to the training data for a change.
atoms.lesson:
The ML engineer owns this step.

Freeze the evaluation set before touching the training data. The freeze is what makes the later candidate-versus-incumbent comparison meaningful, since the split itself must not be influenced by what you did to the training data.
atoms.anchor: 1. Model retraining discipline for this retraining

atoms.obligation: Compare the candidate version against the incumbent on the same frozen evaluation set, and check the differences within each segment.
atoms.lesson: Compare the candidate against the incumbent on the same frozen set, and check the per-stratum deltas, since an aggregate gain frequently hides a regression in the segment a client actually watches.
atoms.anchor: 1. Model retraining discipline for this retraining

atoms.obligation: Verify redistribution rights for every input before publishing anything derived from it, covering licence, derivatives, attribution, and embargo.
atoms.lesson: Verify redistribution rights for each input before publishing anything derived from it: licence, treatment of derivatives, required attribution, embargo period.

atoms.obligation: Escalate any ambiguity about rights or permissions instead of resolving it optimistically in your own favour.
atoms.lesson: Ambiguity is escalated, never resolved optimistically. This applies to each of the four checks on an input: licence, treatment of derivatives, required attribution, embargo period.

atoms.obligation: Keep a small frozen set of cases with known-correct outputs versioned with the code, and compare against it on every change.
atoms.lesson:
The ML engineer owns this step.

Keep a small frozen set of cases with known-correct outputs, versioned with the code, and diff against it on every change.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
atoms.anchor: 3. Validate against a frozen golden set

atoms.obligation: When an expected result legitimately changes, update it in its own separate commit stating the reason, never alongside the behaviour change.
atoms.lesson:
When a golden case legitimately changes, update it in its own commit with the reason in the message — never in the same commit as the behaviour change.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
atoms.anchor: 3. Validate against a frozen golden set

atoms.obligation: Stop and escalate instead of proceeding whenever you cannot satisfy one of the required steps.
atoms.lesson: "If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate." This sentence closes section 3 (Validate against a frozen golden set), section 4 (Baseline: what is required), section 6 (Close against an explicit definition of done), section 7 (Do not over-read small differences) and section 10 (Keep personal and client-confidential data out — non-negotiable). For those steps, inability to comply is an escalation, not a step you work around or skip.
atoms.anchor: 3. Validate against a frozen golden set

atoms.obligation: Take the pre-change measurement under exactly the conditions you will re-measure under before claiming any improvement.
atoms.lesson:
Take the pre-change measurement under exactly the conditions you will re-measure under. Improvement claims without a matched baseline are narrative, not evidence.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.

atoms.obligation: Report every point estimate with an uncertainty band, a note on what the band covers and excludes, and the dominant error term.
atoms.lesson:
Skipping this is the most common way a retraining goes wrong.

Point estimates travel with an uncertainty band and a note on what the band covers and excludes, plus the dominant error term.

atoms.obligation: Disclose uncertainty you cannot quantify in words rather than omitting it from what you report.
atoms.lesson: Unquantifiable uncertainty is disclosed in words, not omitted. Skipping the honest reporting of uncertainty is the most common way a retraining goes wrong.

atoms.obligation: Write the completion criteria before the work starts, so that nothing is added after the fact.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the retraining leaves your hands.

Completion criteria are written first and verified last, item by item, each with its evidence. No post-hoc criteria, no unverifiable ones.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
atoms.anchor: 6. Close against an explicit definition of done

atoms.obligation: Verify each completion criterion at the end, item by item, each with its own evidence, before handing the work on.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the retraining leaves your hands.

Completion criteria are written first and verified last, item by item, each with its evidence. No post-hoc criteria, no unverifiable ones.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
atoms.anchor: 6. Close against an explicit definition of done

atoms.obligation: Compare an apparent difference against the noise floor before claiming it is a real effect.
atoms.lesson:
Compare against the noise floor before claiming an effect: variance across runs, paired arms, a resampling check.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.

atoms.obligation: Report the number of observations next to every mean you present, so readers can judge the difference.
atoms.lesson:
n reported next to every mean. This sits alongside the other noise-floor checks — variance across runs, paired arms, a resampling check — that must precede any claim of an effect.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.

atoms.obligation: Produce a record sufficient for an independent person to re-run the work exactly as you ran it.
atoms.lesson:
Skipping this is the most common way a retraining goes wrong.

Produce a manifest sufficient for an independent re-run: invocation command, image digest, locked dependency set, seeds, and run window.

atoms.obligation: Execute the reproduction record once in a fresh environment to prove it actually works before relying on it.
atoms.lesson: Prove it works by executing it once in a fresh environment; an unverified manifest is a guess. The manifest itself must carry the invocation command, image digest, locked dependency set, seeds, and run window.

atoms.obligation: Estimate the cost of the job before running it, covering processing, storage over its retention, and transfer out.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the retraining leaves your hands.

Cost the job first — compute as unit-count times unit-cost, storage as volume times rate times retention, plus egress.

atoms.obligation: Check the estimated cost against the budget and obtain sign-off when it exceeds the agreed threshold.
atoms.lesson: Check it against the budget, with sign-off above the threshold. Budget overrun is a failure mode, not an externality. Apply this before the retraining leaves your hands.

atoms.obligation: Never propagate personal or confidential fields into shared outputs at any stage of the work.
atoms.lesson:
Apply this before the retraining leaves your hands.

Never propagate personal or client-confidential fields into shared artefacts.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
atoms.anchor: 10. Keep personal and client-confidential data out — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Flag and pause the work if personal or confidential fields turn up in the inputs you receive.
atoms.lesson:
Flag and pause if they turn up in inputs — that is, if personal or client-confidential fields appear in the inputs to the retraining.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
atoms.anchor: 10. Keep personal and client-confidential data out — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Publish aggregated results only with identifiers that cannot be relinked to the underlying individuals or clients.
atoms.lesson:
Publish aggregates with non-relinkable identifiers. Apply this before the retraining leaves your hands.

If you cannot satisfy this, stop and escalate.
atoms.anchor: 10. Keep personal and client-confidential data out — non-negotiable

atoms.obligation: Verify every item on the closing checklist is complete before the work is signed off.
atoms.lesson:
- [ ] Model retraining discipline
- [ ] Check data licensing and redistribution rights
- [ ] Validate against a frozen golden set
- [ ] Measure the current state before changing it
- [ ] Report uncertainty honestly
- [ ] Close against an explicit definition of done
- [ ] Do not over-read small differences
- [ ] Emit a reproducibility manifest
- [ ] Estimate compute and storage cost before running
- [ ] Keep personal and client-confidential data out
